title: DisplayServer.keyboard_get_label_from_physical(keycode) does not handle dead keys properly
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.6.stable

### System information

Godot v4.6.stable.mono - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 3 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8180) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-8700K CPU @ 3.70GHz (12 threads) - 31.93 Gio memory

### Issue description

Calling `DisplayServer.keyboard_get_label_from_physical` with a physical keycode corresponding to a dead key on the active keyboard layout will return the same keycode passed as an argument without doing any conversion. For example, on a Canadian keyboard layout, I would expect `DisplayServer.keyboard_get_label_from_physical(KEY_BRACKETRIGHT)` to return cedilla `¸`, but instead it returns the right bracket `]`, ignoring the keyboard layout entirely. On the other hand, `DisplayServer.keyboard_get_label_from_physical(KEY_SLASH)` correctly returns `É`. The issue seems to only happen with dead keys, and only on Windows.

Looking at the Windows implementation of this method, I found this piece of code:

```cpp
if (ToUnicodeEx(extended_code, scancode, keyboard_state, chars, 255, 4, current_layout) > 0) {
	// ...
}
return p_keycode;
```

The method uses the `ToUnicodeEx` function from winuser.h and, as you can see [here](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-tounicodeex#return-value), it will return a negative value for dead keys. However, Godot only performs the conversion from physical keycode to key label if the returned value is greater than 0, ignoring dead keys and falling back to simply returning the parameter `p_keycode`.

It seems fixing this issue would simply require handling the case where the returned value is negative.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Switch to a Canadian French keyboard layout (https://kbdlayout.info/KBDCA/)
2. Launch the MRP.

### Result

The top label shows the physical right bracket `]` key instead of cedilla `¸`.
The bottom label correctly shows `É` as the label for the physical slash `/` key.


### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[dead-key-issue.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26453168/dead-key-issue.zip)
